translations.text: Then two hundred and three years had passed in the turning of the years, counted by number, and thirty [XXX] more as well, as time is reckoned, winters in the world, since the ruling God, the glory of kings, the light of the righteous, was born into this middle-earth in human form.
It was then the sixth year of Constantine's reign as emperor, since he, the war-leader, had been raised up as army-commander in the kingdom of the Romans.
The shield-protector, bold for his people, was gracious to his warriors. The prince's power grew under the heavens. He was a rightful king, a war-guardian of men.
God strengthened him with glories and with powers, so that throughout the world he became a comfort to many people and a vengeance on nations, once he raised his weapon against enemies.
Battle was offered to him, the noise of war. The people of the Huns and the Hreth-Goths gathered troops; the war-keen Franks and the Hugas marched out.

They were bold men, ready for battle. Spears gleamed, and woven mail-coats. With words and with shields they raised the war-banners. Then the hardy men were openly assembled, and the whole kin together.
The army of the peoples advanced. The wolf in the forest sang a war-song and did not hide the secret of slaughter.

The dewy-feathered eagle raised its song on the track of the enemies. Swiftly the greatest of battle-troops hastened over the city of giants, armies going to war, as many city-warriors of the neighbouring peoples as the king of the Huns could summon to battle anywhere.

The greatest of armies went forth. They drew up their foot-soldiers in mounted companies, so that the spear-brandishers in the foreign host, strong in heart, camped on the bank of the Danube, around the surging of the water.
With the uproar of their host they meant to overwhelm the kingdom of the Romans and plunder it with their armies. There the coming of the Huns became known to the city-dwellers.

Then the emperor ordered that warriors be summoned to battle with great haste, under the flight of arrows, against the fierce fighters, and that his men under the heavens be brought out to the onslaught.
The Romans, warriors famed for victory, were at once equipped with weapons for war, though they had a smaller troop for the battle than the king of the Huns;

They rode around the brave one while the shield resounded and the battle-wood clanged; the king went with his troop, with his army, to war. Above, the raven screamed, dark and fierce for slaughter. The host was on the move.
The horn-bearers leapt forward, the heralds cried out, the horse trod the earth. The army gathered, eager for strife.

The king was afraid, gripped by terror, when he saw the foreign army of the Huns and the Hreth-Goths, that it had assembled a host, a countless force, on the border of the Roman kingdom along the bank of the water.
The king of the Romans bore sorrow of heart; he had no hope for his kingdom for lack of troops. He had too few warriors, shoulder-companions, brave men for battle, against that overwhelming force.
The army encamped, the nobles around the prince, near the river, in close quarters, for the space of a night, after they had first seen the approach of the enemy.
Then, in his sleep, where he slept among his retinue, there was revealed to the emperor himself, the one renowned for victory, the call of a dream.

It seemed to him that someone appeared in the form of a man, beautiful, white and bright of hue, more splendid than any he had seen before or since under the sky. He started up from sleep, covered by his boar-standard.

The messenger, the beautiful herald of glory, quickly spoke to him and called him by name (the helmet of night slipped away): "Constantine, the King of angels, the Ruler of fates, the Lord of hosts, has commanded me to offer you a covenant.
Do not be afraid, though foreigners threaten you with terror and hard battle. Look up to the heavens, to the Guardian of glory; there you will find support, a sign of victory."
At the holy one's command he was at once ready. He unlocked his heart and looked up, as the messenger, the faithful peace-weaver, had told him.
Above the roof of the clouds he saw the beautiful tree of glory, bright with ornaments and adorned with gold (gems glittered). The shining beam was inscribed with letters, bright and radiant:
"With this sign you will overcome the enemy in this perilous danger and hold back the hostile host." Then the light departed, rising upward, and the messenger with it, into the company of the pure.
Because of that fair vision, the king, lord of men, was all the happier and freer from sorrow in his heart.

Then Constantine, the protector of princes, ring-giver to warriors, war-leader of armies, the king blessed with glory, ordered in great haste that a sign, the cross of Christ, be made in the likeness of the beacon he had seen, which had earlier been shown to him in the heavens.

Then before dawn, at the break of day, he ordered the warriors to be roused and the battle-standard to be raised for the clash of weapons, and the holy tree to be carried before him into the midst of the enemies, bearing the sign of God.
There was the crash of shields and the press of men, the hard swinging of swords and the slaughter of armies, once they first met the flight of arrows.

Some barely saved their lives in that campaign. Some fled half-alive into a stronghold and protected their lives among the stone cliffs, holding a place around the Danube. Some were carried off by drowning in the river's current at the end of their lives.
Then the brave troop was full of joy. They pursued the foreign peoples from daybreak on until evening.
Ash-wood spears flew, serpents of battle. The troop was cut down, the shield-band of the hated enemy. Only a few of the Huns' army came back home from there.

Then the protector of armies went back home from there, exulting in his plunder (the battle was decided), honoured by war. Then the protector of warriors came with a troop of thanes to seek his mighty dwelling; the king, brave in battle, came to visit his cities.

When those who had been instructed through baptism learned that they were allowed to make known the gift of the gospel before the emperor (their minds were light and their spirits rejoiced, though they were few),

He released the children of men, the sad spirits, from the prison of devils, and gave them grace through that same created thing that had been shown to him in a vision, the sign of victory against the attack of nations.
And how on the third day the glory of men, the Lord of all the race of men, arose from the tomb and from death, and ascended to heaven.
Then the giver of treasure, the battle-hardened king, was joyful. A new joy was placed in his heart. The guardian of the heavenly kingdom was his greatest comfort and the closest of his hopes.
Then through the gift of the Spirit he began eagerly to proclaim the law of the Lord day and night. The gold-friend of men, spear-brave and unwearying, truly devoted himself to the service of God.

Then through learned teachers the prince, protector of the people, hardened in battle and bold with the spear, found in God's books where the Ruler of the heavens had been hanged on the cross-tree amid the clamour of the crowd, out of envy, through malice,
Then they let the foamy, high-prowed sea-horses glide over the ocean. Over the tossing sea, the ship's side was often struck by the blows of the waves. The sea resounded.

At the shore they left the ships, the old wave-houses, washed by the sand and held fast by anchors, to wait on the water for the men's return, until the warrior-queen and her troop of men would come back to them over the eastern ways.
The bold soldiers, the emperor's messengers, warriors dressed in armour, went eagerly into the land of the Greeks.

Then she ordered that the wisest of the city-dwellers far and wide among the Jews be summoned, each of the men, to come to a council and take counsel: those who could most deeply explain the mysteries of the Lord through the true law.
who can truly tell me and give answer on your behalf from now on about each of the matters that I ask of them."

Concerning this, King David sang a lordly song, the wise prophet of old, father of Solomon, and the leader of warriors spoke this word: 'I have seen before me the God of beginnings, the Lord of victories.
"Often you have done foolish deeds, accursed exiles, and despised the scriptures, the teaching of the fathers, but never more than now,
"Now go quickly and seek out separately those among you who have the most wisdom, strength and skill of mind, so that they may boldly tell me, without hesitation, each thing that I seek from them."

"I know well that she wants to inquire about the tree of victory on which the ruler of nations suffered, free of all sins, God's own Son, whom, guiltless of every crime, our fathers hanged out of hatred on the high tree in days of old.
'If it should happen to you in your lifetime that you hear wise men ask about the holy tree and raise disputes about the tree of victory on which the true King was hanged,
the guardian of the heavenly kingdom, the child of all peace, then make it known quickly, my dear son, before death takes you.
Then you will earn eternal life, the best of the rewards of victory, which will be given to you in heaven.'
They were ready, sad at heart, the protectors of the people, when they had been summoned by a stern decree; they went to the court and made known the power of their learning.

Then the queen began to address the Hebrew men, to question the weary-spirited men about the ancient scriptures: how in the world the prophets, men holy in spirit, had sung long before about the Son of God, where the Lord suffered, the true Son of the Creator, for love of souls.
but they denied every word that she began to ask, firm in their minds, and said that never in their lives, before or since, had they heard anything of the kind.
Elene spoke and answered them in anger: "I will tell you truly, and it will not prove a lie while you live: if you go on any longer with this falsehood, with deceitful fraud,

…who stand before me, that fire on a hill will consume you, the hottest of fierce flames, and the leaping flame will destroy your corpses, so that this falsehood will be repaid to you with your parting from the world.
You cannot make good those words which you have for a while now wrongfully hidden under coverings of sin; you cannot hide the event or conceal the deep power."

Then they expected death, the pyre and the end of their lives, and there they handed over one man who was well versed in sayings (his name was Judas, given him by his kinsmen); they gave him to the queen and said that he was exceptionally wise:
"He can make the truth known to you and reveal the mystery of events as you question him in words, rightly from the beginning on to the end.
On earth he is of noble lineage, wise in the craft of words and a prophet's son, bold in council. It is natural to him to have wise answers and skill in his heart.
Before the multitude of men he will make known to you the gift of wisdom through the great power, as your mind desires."

She let each of them go in peace to seek his own home, and took that one man, Judas, as a hostage, and then earnestly asked him to teach the truth about the cross, which had long been hidden in its resting place, and she called him aside by himself.

Elene, the glorious queen, spoke to the solitary man: "Two things are ready for you, life or death, whichever you would rather choose. Make known quickly now what you are willing to agree to in this matter."
Judas answered her in turn (he could not escape the distress or turn aside the hostility of the king [?]; he was in the queen's power):
"How can it happen to a man who treads the moorland in the wilderness, weary and without food, held captive by hunger, when bread and stone both come into his sight together,
the hard and the soft, that he would take the stone as protection against hunger, pay no heed to the bread, turn to want and refuse the food, and scorn the better, when he has the use of both?"
Then the blessed Helen gave him an answer openly before the noblemen: "If you wish to have a dwelling with the angels in the heavenly kingdom, and life on earth,
and a reward of victory in heaven, tell me quickly where the cross of the King of heaven lies, holy under the earth, which for some time now you have hidden from men through the sin of murder."

Judas spoke (his mind was sad and hot at heart, and he dreaded both choices: that he should give up the hope of the heavenly kingdom and also this present realm under the heavens, and that he should not reveal the cross):
"How can I find what happened so long ago, through the passing of the years? Many have now gone by, two hundred [CC] or more counted in number.
I cannot tell it, since I do not know the number."
There are now many wise and good men, men of understanding, who were before us and have since passed away.
I was born afterwards, in later days, a young man, still a youth. I cannot find in my mind what I do not know, what happened so long ago."
Elene spoke to him in answer: "How has it come about among this people that you know in memory so fully every one of the deeds that the Trojans did in battle?
That open ancient war was much further back in the course of years than this noble event.
You can readily and quickly recount how many in all, in number of men, were slain there, spear-fighters fallen dead behind the shield-wall.
"You set down in writing the graves under the rocky slopes, and the place too, and the count of the years."
Judas spoke, bearing grievous sorrow: "We remember that warfare closely, my lady, out of necessity,
and we set down in writing the violence of battle and the conduct of the peoples; but we have never heard this made known to men from any man's mouth, except here now."

The noble queen gave him answer: "You deny too strongly the truth and what is right about the tree of life. Only a little while ago you spoke truly about the tree of victory to your people, and now you turn to a lie."
Judas answered her in turn and said that he had spoken it in distress and very much in doubt, expecting for himself a lesser affliction.
The emperor's kinswoman quickly answered him: "Listen, we have heard it made known to men through holy books that the noble son of the King was hanged on Calvary, the spiritual Son of God.
You must, in reply, reveal the knowledge, as the writings say, of where on the plain the place of Calvary is, before death takes you and you perish for your sins,

so that afterwards I may cleanse it according to Christ's will, as a help to men, so that holy God, the mighty Lord, the giver of glory to the hosts, the helper of souls, may fulfil for me the intent of my life, my desire."
Judas answered her stubbornly: "I do not know the place, and I know nothing of the plain or of the circumstances."

Helen spoke with earnest mind: "I swear by the Son of the Creator, the God who was hanged, that you shall be tormented with hunger in front of your kinsmen unless you give up these lies and tell me the truth plainly."

Then she commanded that he be led away alive by the troop, and the guilty man shoved (the servants did not delay) into a dry pit, where, without any comforts, he lingered in sorrow for the space of seven nights in that prison, tormented by hunger,
bound in fetters, and then on the seventh day, afflicted with pains, weary and without food, he began to call out (his strength was diminished):
"I beg you by the God of the heavens to let me up out of these hardships, humbled as I am by the torment of hunger.

Then, resolute, they went to the place, up onto the hill where the Lord had once been hanged, the Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, the Son of God on the gallows. And yet he, humbled by hunger, did not know for certain

and you measured with your hands the whole circuit of the earth and the sky above, and you yourself sit, Ruler of victories, above the noblest race of angels, who travel through the air surrounded by light, in great majesty.
Heaven and earth and all the high powers are full of this glory, marked with honour.' Two among them, a victorious race in the sky, are called seraphim by name.
over which you, Lord God, rule forever; and you cast out of the heavens the sinful, guilt-working, reckless enemies.

Then that accursed band had to fall beneath dark dwellings into the ruin of torments, where they now suffer death-agony in the surging fire, in the dragon's embrace, wrapped in darkness. He had rejected your sovereignty.
Just as you heard the holy man Moses when he spoke, when you, God of might, at that noble time revealed to the man the bones of Joseph beneath the hillside, so I [ask] you,
Then from that place a vapour rose up like smoke under the heavens. At this the man's heart was lifted up. Blessed and wise in the law, he clapped both hands upward.
Thanks be to you without end, God of hosts, enthroned in glory, that through your glory you have revealed to me, so unworthy and so sinful, the mysteries of what has happened.
He took hold of the joyful tree of glory with his hands, and with the company raised it from its grave in the earth. The travellers on foot, the nobles, went into the city.
The queen rejoiced in her heart at the deed, and then began to ask on which of the trees the Son of the Ruler, the giver of hope to men, had been hanged:
Then praise was raised fairly among the people. They honoured the Father, and praised in words the true Son of the Ruler. To him be glory and thanks forever without end from all creation!

Then the devil of hell began to cry out, the terrible monster, intent on evil: "Lo, what man is this who once again, through the ancient strife, destroys my following, increases the old enmity, and plunders my possessions?

Lo, the Saviour has often shut me up in the narrow home, to my sorrow in my misery! Through Judas I once became hopeful, and now I am humbled, stripped of goods, through Judas again, outlawed and friendless.

Yet afterwards I can find a way back out of the dens of the damned through accusations. I will rouse against you another king, who will persecute you, and he will abandon your teaching and follow my wicked customs,
and he will then send you into the blackest and worst terrors of torment, so that, afflicted by pains, you will firmly renounce the crucified King whom you once obeyed."

Then wise-minded Judas, the man brave in battle, answered him (the Holy Spirit had been firmly entrusted to him, fire-hot love, surging understanding through a prophet's wisdom), and spoke these words, full of wisdom:

Her heart was the gladder because she heard that the fiend of hell, the dispenser of sins, was overcome. And then she marvelled at the man's wisdom: how he, who had been so ignorant, had in so short a time become so full of faith, steeped in wisdom.

At that welcome news his heart laughed, and it was the greatest comfort that had come to him in the world. The army-leaders, his messengers, brought it to him over the eastern ways: the men had made a safe journey with the victorious queen over the swan-road to the land of the Greeks.
He commanded that greeting be sent to Elene, brave in battle, if they had come through the sea and been allowed to make a safe journey, those bold-spirited men, to the holy city.

There the holy cross had been found, the most glorious of trees that earth-dwellers have heard of on the earthly way. She did so, after kinsmen and friends had brought many welcome tidings from the west over the fastness of the sea.
Then he was baptized who for many seasons before [?] light ready [?]. His heart was inspired toward the better life and turned to glory.

The queen of the Christians began to ask about this. She asked Cyriacus to fulfil her wish once more, by the powers of the Spirit, concerning a wondrous event, and to reveal it through glorious gifts. She spoke these words to the bishop, speaking boldly:
"You, protector of men, have rightly shown me the noble tree, the cross of the King of the heavens, on which the helper of souls was hanged by heathen hands, God's own Son, the Saviour of men.
I wish that you would find those things that are still hidden in the earth, buried deep, concealed in darkness.
My mind keeps grieving and mourns in sorrow. It will not rest until the almighty Father, Lord of hosts, Saviour of men, fulfils my desire, holy from on high, through the finding of the nails.
Now, best of messengers, quickly and in all humility send your prayer into the bright creation, into the joy of glory.
Pray to the Majesty of hosts that the almighty King may reveal to you the hoard under the earth, which still lies hidden, secret from men, and waits in concealment."

Then suddenly a leaping flame came, brighter than the sun. The people saw their gracious Giver make known a wonder. There, out of the darkness, the nails shone up from below out of their narrow place, lying close to the ground, and gleamed with light like the stars of heaven or golden gems.
Then the bishop of that people was gladdened anew, he who had turned to salvation through the Son of God.
She knelt, bright in faith [?], and honoured the gift, exulting with joy, that had been brought to her as relief from her afflictions.

Then, through spiritual mysteries, she began to seek eagerly in her mind the way of truth to glory. Indeed the God of hosts, the Father in the heavens, the almighty King, helped her, so that the queen gained her desire in the world.
The prophecy had been sung beforehand by the sages of old, all of it from the beginning, just as it later came to pass in every matter.

Through the gift of the Spirit, the queen of the people began to inquire eagerly, closely and often, how she could best and most worthily use the nails, as a comfort to the hosts, and what the Lord's will was in this.
She then ordered that a very wise man be brought to her quickly for counsel, one wise in spirit who, through his keen ability, knew well how to give advice,
and she began to ask him what seemed best to him to do in this matter, and she chose to follow his teaching on behalf of the people.
'That sign will be called holy to God, and so will the bold and blessed one, honoured in war, whom that steed carries.'"

Then Elene quickly carried all of that out before the nobles. She ordered the prince's bridle to be adorned, the bridle of the ring-giver of men, and sent it over the ocean stream as a gift to her own son, a flawless gift.
Then the queen began to teach the beloved company that they should firmly keep the love of the Lord, and likewise peace and friendship among themselves, without fault, throughout their lives,

I often had the tree of glory in my thoughts, not just once, before I had revealed the wonder of the bright tree, as I found it made known in books, in the course of events, in writings about the sign of victory.
Therefore they now shine in beauty like the angels, and enjoy the inheritance of the King of glory forever. Amen.
